Incident Date:	11/11/2025

2/19/26 4:05 AM	Page 2 of 4

Description:	I scheduled an intake via telehealth with Dr. Inderpreet Virk, operating as the lead psychiatrist for Brain Health USA. I sought care based on the clinic's explicit advertisements stating they specialize in complex substance issues and benzodiazepine tapering. I presented seeking a safe, medically supervised taper off of street-sourced Xanax (historically up to 22mg, at the time of meeting, 6mg).

Despite being a Board-Certified Addiction Psychiatrist, Dr. Virk exhibited a severe departure from the standard of care:

Refusal to Treat / Patient Abandonment: Dr. Virk explicitly refused to initiate a standard medical tapering protocol, stating my case was "too much of a liability" and a "sticky situation" because my prior usage was street-sourced and lacked pharmaceutical documentation. Refusing to medically manage a patient actively seeking to transition from illicit benzodiazepines to safe medical oversight—while knowing the fatal risks of abrupt benzodiazepine withdrawal—constitutes gross negligence and a fundamental failure to perform the duties of an addiction specialist.

Misleading Advertising (Bait-and-Switch): Brain Health USA specifically advertises specialized benzodiazepine tapering to Medi-Cal/L.A. Care patients. However, their lead addiction psychiatrist outright refuses to treat patients with a history of street procurement, which encompasses a massive demographic of the addiction population they claim to serve.

Substandard Psychiatric Assessment: After denying primary care for the benzodiazepine dependency, Dr. Virk reluctantly prescribed a 10-day Suboxone bridge at my desperate request. He then concluded the session by rapidly asking if I felt suicidal or felt like hurting or others, utilizing a dismissive, "box-checking" approach to a severe psychiatric safety assessment for a highly vulnerable patient he had just denied comprehensive care to.

I request the Board investigate Dr. Virk's refusal to provide standard addiction medicine care, his patient abandonment due to "liability," and the misleading nature of the clinic's advertised specialties.
